observations: Yellow and black plastic housing for a portable battery charger.
Digital LCD display is active in photo 0, showing '13.8V' and a battery icon.
Brand name 'ANHTCZUX' is visible on the front panel and back label.
Model 'Zyx-J10' is printed on the technical specification label in photo 2.
Red and black alligator clips are attached to the unit.
Label specifies compatibility with 12V batteries from 4Ah to 100Ah.
Output is rated at 13.8V - 15.5V with a maximum of 6A.

claims.claim: Intelligent smart pulse car battery charger
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows 'PULSE REPAIR CHARGER' text and an LCD interface.
While it displays voltage, there is no dedicated testing interface or load test capability shown.
The label in photo 2 specifies 12V 4Ah-100Ah, which typically excludes 24V systems and may not support lithium types without specific labeling.

risks.risk: The unit powers on but fails to deliver charging current to a battery.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit connected to a depleted battery with the display indicating active charging (Amps/Current flow).

risks.risk: Internal cooling fan is seized or noisy, leading to overheating.
risks.proof: A video with sound while the unit is under load.

risks.risk: Internal wire breaks or poor contact at the alligator clips.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the cable entry points and the clip teeth.

proof_requests: Video of the charger connected to a car battery showing the charging current (Amps) on the display.
Video with audio to confirm the cooling fan is operational and quiet.
Close-up photo of the power plug to confirm compatibility with local sockets.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified by brand and model. Although it powers on, its ability to actually charge a battery is unproven, so it is priced at its worst case.
